target_state: Fresh package, no prior staging work and no ownership-ledger entry for this VA. The whole body is 11 instructions and 30 bytes and was re-read from the image for this package rather than taken on trust: GhidraMCP /read_memory at 0x0057d6f0 for 30 bytes returns 56 8b f1 e8 28 c7 ff ff f6 44 24 08 01 74 09 56 e8 7b 9c 9c 00 83 c4 04 8b c6 5e c2 04 00, and /disassemble_function returns those same 11 instructions at those same 11 addresses. The instruction lengths 1+2+5+5+2+1+5+3+2+1+3 give 30, independently of ghidra_function.body_span_bytes, and abi_derived.parse reports {declared_count 11, unparsed 0, degraded false, flow_complete true}, so the 11 are the whole body and not a slice. This package reconstructs all of it: both direct calls in their machine order, the single-bit test of one byte of the one stack argument, the branch, the caller-side stack adjustment around the second call, the callee-side 4-byte cleanup at the terminator, and the receiver returned in EAX. It does NOT resolve the receiver's IDENTITY: whether the incoming ECX points at the head of an object or at an interior sub-object is not visible from this body, and that remains an open question below. The calling convention, by contrast, IS now resolved: the ABI oracle gained rule R1-VFT, and the derived record for this target now DETERMINES __thiscall at INFERRED confidence (conventions.calling_convention = __thiscall, confidence = INFERRED, candidate_conventions = [__thiscall], ambiguities = []), with the cleanup separately OBSERVED (cleanup.bytes 4, cleanup.side callee, cleanup.evidence "ret 0x4"). The reconstructed entry is a naked __thiscall transcription of the binary's own thirty bytes, so the source span carries the token the validator reads.

intended_paths.status: staging-only handoff; src/ is integrator-owned and was not touched

vtables.role: the body occupies displacement +0x08 of this table; read out of the table's own bytes, and it is the same table 0x00579e20 installs at the receiver's offset 0 as its first act. No slot is named and no class is claimed.

implementation.calling_convention_in_the_source: __thiscall (naked, on the entry the validator binds to 0x0057d6f0; spelled once as the macro PKG_EDITOR_W1_0057D6F0_NAKED_THISCALL, which expands to __attribute__((naked, thiscall)))
implementation.calling_convention_evidence: THE PACK'S, and now determinate. abi_derived for this target states conventions.calling_convention = __thiscall, conventions.confidence = INFERRED, conventions.candidate_conventions = ["__thiscall"], conventions.ambiguities = [], verdict ABI_INFERRED; receiver {present true, register ECX, provenance vftable_slot_dispatch, confidence INFERRED, bounds_only true, shape null, distinct_offsets 0, written_through 0}; cleanup {bytes 4, side "callee", evidence "ret 0x4", confidence OBSERVED}. The determination is made in two recorded steps. R1-VFT puts the receiver in ECX because this address is a slot (displacement +0x08) of the sound vptr-backed vftable based at 0x013f57f8 and because the body READS the register that dispatch delivered -- the record states the discriminator explicitly: a body in the COM / __stdcall shape takes its receiver from the first popped stack word and never reads its incoming ECX. C6B then names __thiscall from the callee-side cleanup together with that receiver register. The receiver alias the older record could not use is not needed: R1-VFT works off the table slot, not off a dereference. This is an INFERRED determination and is reported as one; nothing in this repository has observed a caller dispatching through the table. Caller-side corroboration, which the record itself lists as "corroboration": "not_available", is supplied here from the entry paths read from the image: every code reference to 0x0057d6f0 other than the table slot at 0x013f5800 is the JMP of a two-instruction this-adjusting stub (GhidraMCP /disassemble_bytes over 0x0057a590..0x0057a5d3): 0x0057a5a0 SUB ECX,0x10 ; 0x0057a5a3 JMP 0x0057d6f0 / 0x0057a5b0 SUB ECX,0x14 ; 0x0057a5b3 JMP 0x0057d6f0 / 0x0057a5c0 SUB ECX,0x4 ; 0x0057a5c3 JMP 0x0057d6f0. A first argument that a caller-side stub reduces by a constant before the transfer is a receiver; a by-value parameter is not adjusted. __stdcall is excluded on the same evidence (a free function has no receiver for a caller-side stub to adjust) and __fastcall is excluded because the terminator is RET 0x4 and the body reads no register argument other than ECX.
implementation.receiver_type_note: Declared but deliberately NOT defined. This body never dereferences its incoming register: it copies the value, hands that value to two other routines, and puts it in EAX. There is no load and no store through the receiver anywhere in the 11 instructions, so no offset, no member, no size and no layout of the object is claimed here, and the struct carries none. (0x00579e20 reaches to +0x5f8 of its own receiver; that is the callee's knowledge and it is not imported.)
implementation.argument_surface: a receiver in ECX and exactly one ordinary stack argument, a 32-bit option word at entry_ESP+0x4, of which the body reads ONE BIT: bit 0 of its LOW byte, through `TEST byte ptr [ESP + 0x8],0x1` at 0x0057d6f8. The other 31 bits are read by no instruction in this body. The slot is not written by this body and nothing is written through a pointer. The model's test drives 0x2, 0x4, 0x100, 0x10000, 0x1000000, 0x80000000 and 0xdeadbe00 as well as 0x0, 0x1, 0x3, 0xdeadbe01 and 0xffffffff, so 'any nonzero', 'bit 1', 'the sign bit' and 'a high byte' are each refuted by the measurement.
implementation.return_type_note: That spelling is the machine fact rather than a choice: the value the listing leaves in EAX is the receiver, carried in ESI across both calls and written back with MOV EAX,ESI at 0x0057d708, which both paths reach. A pointer is also the width-computable spelling, and the machine return state is WIDTH_4_IN_EAX off the complete listing (see validation). It is NOT void: the record's return_semantics 'unclassified_in_EAX' with RT2 register_class 'aggregate_unknown' is a statement about the record, and the listing shows a value plainly.
implementation.callee_model: two out-of-line calls, declared in the package header and DEFINED BY THE MODEL TEST as observers, because the body under test has to call something and this package claims nothing about either callee's internals. teardown_00579e20: entered with the object in ECX and nothing on the stack, ends in a bare RET. dispose_00f47380: entered with one cdecl dword on the stack, ends in a bare RET at 0x00f47394, which is why the model needs no cleanup after it (the listing has ADD ESP,0x4 at 0x0057d705 for exactly that reason). Because the entry is a naked transcription, both calls are named from inside the assembly block, and the model test RESOLVES each emitted rel32 and requires it to land on the callee the xref export names for that callsite -- so 'the right callee' is a constraint on the emitted code rather than a comment on it.
implementation.dispatch_model: none, and none declared. abi_derived.dispatch records indirect_calls 0, call_offsets [] and vtable_shaped_loads 0, and the 11 instructions contain no register- or memory-operand transfer: both transfers are CALLs with an immediate operand. The body is itself a table slot occupant, which is the opposite of dispatching -- it never reads the word at the receiver's +0x00 -- so no slot is modelled as a member and no dispatch pointer is declared.
implementation.control_flow_model: one conditional branch, `JZ 0x0057d708`, whose target is the common tail. Two basic blocks. No loop, no second exit, no path that misses the epilogue.
implementation.stack_discipline_model: callee-side cleanup of 4 bytes, re-derived from the three terminators' forms rather than read off the record: 0x00579e20 ends in POP ESI / POP EBX / POP ECX / RET (bare), 0x00f47380 ends in RET (bare, C3 at 0x00f47394), and this body ends in RET 0x4 (C2 04 00 at 0x0057d70b). The model test MEASURES the balance on ESP either side of the call through a bare-assembly probe that touches only EAX, ECX and EDX, in both directions: against a caller-cleaned cdecl twin handed the SAME two pushes, the two stack-pointer deltas differ by exactly the RET immediate and by nothing else. The twin returns its own EAX sentinel, so the check also shows the probe really reads EAX and that the two bodies did not come back the same. It also measures the balance with a decoy dword below the argument.
implementation.globals_model: none. No instruction in the body names a data-segment address; the only address-valued immediates are the two call targets 0x00579e20 and 0x00f47380, both inside .text. The record's globals category is empty and the xref export carries no data-reference edge for this VA. (0x00579e20 and 0x00f47380 do name absolute addresses -- 0x013f57f8 and 0x015e4ef0 in the first, 0x016c8b44 in the second -- and none of them is imported here.)
implementation.compile_gate: Every configuration is a real build followed by a real run, not a compile alone. g++ 16.2.1 and clang++ 22.1.8, each at -O0, -O1, -O2, -O3 and -Os, each with -m32 -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fPIC: ten builds, all clean, all exiting 0. The same ten were also built with -fno-pic and run, and the two -O0/-O2 -fno-pic outputs additionally linked with -no-pie; all ten ran to exit 0. The header compiles clean on its own under both compilers. The entry is a naked __thiscall function, which is what the derived ABI record names (INFERRED, rule C6B on rule R1-VFT), and it emits the binary's thirty bytes: the model test pins eighteen byte positions literally against kTargetBytes (the /read_memory transcript), accepts each of two accepted encodings for the two register moves (8b f1 / 89 ce and 8b c6 / 89 f0 -- the register-move direction, which the GNU assembler spells the other way round and clang++ does not), and RESOLVES both CALL rel32 displacements to require that each lands on the callee the xref export names for that callsite. A ten-byte __x86.get_pc_thunk.ax PC anchor, which g++ -m32 -fPIC can prepend to a naked function, is recognised by its exact opcode pair e8 ?? ?? ?? ?? 05 and the thirty target bytes are required immediately after it; byte-identical recompilation is NOT claimed without that allowance and no other allowance exists. The call harness was rewritten as one bare-assembly block with its own EBP frame that touches only EAX, ECX and EDX. The previous revision kept its two call-surviving samples in ESI and EDI and spent EBX as a scratch push register; both were OUTPUT directions and so were safe in themselves, but the EBX clobber was a latent hazard on a PIC i386 build, where EBX holds the GOT base, and none of it was necessary. A hand-written probe that borrows a callee-saved register and never restores it corrupts its CALLER and fails only from -O1 upwards -- the defect the sibling package for 0x0052e650 still carries -- and this probe cannot make it.
implementation.mutation_gate: The model test was mutation-verified, not merely run. THIRTY-FOUR wrong reconstructions were planted one at a time, each on its own copy of the package, and each was built and run under g++ and clang++ at -O0 and -O2 -- four configurations per mutation. All thirty-four died in all four; the unmutated control was clean in all four. What was planted, and the checks that killed each (the first four named): the terminator's immediate removed (ret 0, caller cleans up) -- A8, H5, I1, I3; the terminator's immediate widened (ret 8) -- A8, H5, I1, I3; the TEST mask changed from 0x1 to 0x2 -- A1, A3, A6, B10; the TEST mask changed to 0x100 -- A1, A3, A6, B10; the MOV ESI,ECX replaced by a self-XCHG, so ECX is clobbered by the first call -- A6, A7, B0, B10; the JZ replaced by JMP (dispose becomes unconditional) -- A1, A3, A6, B10; the JZ deleted entirely -- B0, B2, B4, B5; the two calls exchanged in order -- A10, A11, A2, A5; the teardown call replaced by a second dispose call -- A10, A11, A2, A5; the dispose's argument changed from ESI to ECX, as an adjustor would -- A6, E0, E1, E2; the ADD ESP,0x4 at 0x0057d705 deleted, leaving the second callee's word unpopped -- died (stack corruption); the POP ESI moved above the tail -- A7, B0, B10, B11; the tail made to compute something else before MOV EAX,ESI -- W13, W14, W3, W4b; the stack read moved from [ESP+0x8] to [ESP+0x4] -- A1, A3, A6, B10; the record's confidence upgraded to OBSERVED -- L3; the record's confidence dropped to UNKNOWN -- L3; the cleanup-side enumerator reordered so kCaller is 0 -- L10a; the cleanup-side constant flipped off kCallee -- L10; the cleanup byte count 4 -> 8 -- I4, L10b; the RET immediate 4 -> 8 -- L10c, M3a, M3b; the receiver's dereference count claimed as 1 -- L8a; the receiver's provenance falsified -- L9a; the candidate-convention count 1 -> 2 -- L2a; kTargetBytes' RET immediate byte 04 -> 08 -- W3; kTargetBytes' JZ displacement 09 -> 0a -- W3; kTargetBytes' TEST mask 01 -> 02 -- W3; kTargetBytes' POP ESI opcode 5e -> 90 -- W3; the teardown observer recording a corrupted pointer -- A5, E0, E1, E2; the teardown observer recording nothing -- A1, A2, A3, A5; the dispose observer recording nothing -- A1, A3, A6, B10; the caller-cleaned twin made to pop a word after all -- died (stack corruption); the probe made to sample ESP one word too high -- A8, H5, I1, I3. No check compares a value with itself: every expected value is either a literal written out in the case, or a byte taken from kTargetBytes, which is the binary's own /read_memory output. In particular the emitted bytes are compared against kTargetBytes and never against a second assembly of the same instructions, because two assemblies agreeing with each other is implied by both being pinned to the binary and would only look like coverage. The caller-cleaned twin in the cleanup case exists so that 'callee pops four bytes' is a measured difference between two bodies driven through one harness rather than a restatement of the RET immediate; it returns its own EAX sentinel so the harness channel is shown to be real, and a twin that pops a word dies.
implementation.side_of_cleanup: callee, 4 bytes, confirmed by the terminator's own form (C2 04 00) and re-derived from the stack arithmetic in the model, and MEASURED on ESP by the model test in both directions: a `ret 0` and a `ret 8` are both refuted, and so is a twin that claims to be caller-cleaned while popping a word. The convention and the cleanup are carried as two separate facts, because __thiscall does not by itself settle who pops; the observed side is the terminator. The ADD ESP,0x4 at 0x0057d705 belongs to the second callee only, which is cdecl; it is not this body's argument cleanup.

function_extent.listing_reexported: GhidraMCP /read_memory at 0x0057d6f0 for 30 bytes, and /disassemble_function at 0x0057d6f0 returning 11 instructions at 0x0057d6f0 PUSH ESI (56), 0x0057d6f1 MOV ESI,ECX (8b f1), 0x0057d6f3 CALL 0x00579e20 (e8 28 c7 ff ff), 0x0057d6f8 TEST byte ptr [ESP + 0x8],0x1 (f6 44 24 08 01), 0x0057d6fd JZ 0x0057d708 (74 09), 0x0057d6ff PUSH ESI (56), 0x0057d700 CALL 0x00f47380 (e8 7b 9c 9c 00), 0x0057d705 ADD ESP,0x4 (83 c4 04), 0x0057d708 MOV EAX,ESI (8b c6), 0x0057d70a POP ESI (5e), 0x0057d70b RET 0x4 (c2 04 00). 1+2+5+5+2+1+5+3+2+1+3 = 30 = ghidra_function.body_span_bytes, and 0x0057d70d is ghidra_function.body_end. abi_derived.parse: {declared_count 11, unparsed 0, degraded false, flow_complete true, esp_unresolved false, local_extent 0, layout json_instruction_list, frame: no push_ebp, no mov_ebp_esp, no sub, fp false, ebp_is_general_register false}.
function_extent.frame: none. No prologue, no SUB ESP, no PUSH EBP, no EBP frame, nothing spilled. Exactly one register is saved: ESI, pushed at 0x0057d6f0 and popped at 0x0057d70a, a save/restore pair bracketing the whole body. The body's entire local state is that one register, and it exists because the call at 0x0057d6f3 would otherwise destroy ECX.

observed_original_abi.receiver_alias: ESI. MOV ESI,ECX at 0x0057d6f1 is the only copy, and the copy exists to survive the two calls, not to reach a field: the body never dereferences ESI, so the alias buys lifetime and nothing else. That is exactly what the derived receiver record states -- bounds_only true, shape null, distinct_offsets 0, written_through 0 -- and it is why no field offset is claimed here either. The alias is NOT the reason the record now names a receiver: R1-VFT works from the vftable slot and the fact that the body READS the incoming ECX, and the caller-side this-adjusting stubs corroborate it independently.
observed_original_abi.receiver_note: the body addresses NO byte of the receiver, so there is no displacement, no field and no size to record. The receiver record's empty offsets list is correct here, not a gap in the pack.
observed_original_abi.stack_argument_1: a 32-bit word at entry_ESP+0x4. The read is a BYTE read of its low byte, one bit of that: `TEST byte ptr [ESP + 0x8],0x1` at 0x0057d6f8, where [ESP + 0x8] is entry_ESP + 4 because the PUSH ESI at 0x0057d6f0 is still in effect and 0x00579e20 restores ESP with a bare RET. The slot is not written and nothing is written through a pointer. The meaning of the word and of its other 31 bits is not fixed by anything in this body.
observed_original_abi.stack_argument_2: none, and not because the terminator says so: no instruction in the body has an ESP-relative operand other than the one TEST, and a decoy dword planted at entry_ESP+0x8 changes nothing in the model test.
observed_original_abi.return_observation: The record classifies the last write to EAX as aggregate_unknown (RT2) and the envelope as unclassified_in_EAX. The listing says more than that and this package reads only the listing: the single write to EAX is MOV EAX,ESI at 0x0057d708, a register-to-register move of the value ESI has held since 0x0057d6f1, so the returned value is the incoming receiver verbatim and 32 bits wide. Both paths to the single reachable RET pass through 0x0057d708, so the must-analysis has no uninitialised path. The C type is Receiver *, which is the width-computable spelling of a 4-byte value that the machine shows to be the receiver; the exact C spelling is a source-side choice and the machine fixes only the width and the fact that it is the pointer it was given.
observed_original_abi.calling_convention_determination: C6B, on the receiver rule R1-VFT. conventions.calling_convention = __thiscall, conventions.confidence = INFERRED, conventions.candidate_conventions = ["__thiscall"], conventions.ambiguities = [], verdict ABI_INFERRED. R1-VFT: this address is slot displacement +0x08 of the sound vptr-backed vftable based at 0x013f57f8 and the body READS the register the dispatch delivered (receiver_register ECX, receiver_provenance vftable_slot_dispatch, cleanup_side callee), which is the shape R1-VFT discriminates from a COM / __stdcall body. C6B: the callee pops its own stack argument, which rules out cdecl and fastcall, and the receiver arrives in ECX. INFERRED, not OBSERVED: nothing here has watched a caller dispatch through the table.
observed_original_abi.receiver: ECX carries the receiver. The record says so at INFERRED confidence: receiver {present true, register ECX, provenance vftable_slot_dispatch, bounds_only true, shape null, distinct_offsets 0, written_through 0}. In the body itself the receiver is read once, MOV ESI,ECX at 0x0057d6f1, and aliased into ESI so that it survives both calls; the SAME VALUE then goes to 0x00579e20 in ECX (unchanged) and to 0x00f47380 on the stack (unchanged), and what MOV EAX,ESI at 0x0057d708 writes into EAX is that value and nothing else. It is NOT dereferenced anywhere in the eleven instructions: there is no load and no store through it in any register, so no field offset, no displacement, no member, no size and no layout is claimed, and the record's empty offsets list with bounds_only true is the correct reading rather than a gap.
observed_original_abi.receiver_identity: UNRESOLVED. __thiscall says where the receiver arrives, not what it is. This body neither dereferences nor adjusts the pointer, and it is reached through three stubs that adjust ECX by 0x10, 0x14 and 0x4, so at least three different base relationships reach it. No class, no vtable identity, no receiver type and no object size is claimed.
observed_original_abi.conventions_note: The convention is recorded because the MACHINE now determines it, not because this package chose it. The determination is transcribed field for field from evidence pack category abi_derived and is carried in the staging header as data (kDerivedConventionVerdict, kDerivedConventionConfidence, kCandidateConventionCount, kDerivedReceiverRegister, kReceiverProvenance, kObservedCleanupSide), where the model test checks each value against an independently written literal. Nothing was weakened, disabled or special-cased to reach any validator verdict, and no convention was invented: the previous revision of this sidecar deliberately carried NO convention field at all, precisely because the record then abstained (verdict ABI_UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN, reason ecx_read_without_deref). That abstention is gone; it is not being papered over.
observed_original_abi.corroboration_of_the_unchosen_candidate: __stdcall was the former other candidate and it is excluded by the same three entry stubs: a free function has no receiver for a caller-side stub to adjust by a constant, and a stub that adjusted a by-value first argument would be adjusting a value it had already computed. __fastcall is not a candidate at all: the terminator is RET 0x4 (the callee pops), and the body reads no register argument other than ECX.
observed_original_abi.variadic: UNKNOWN in the pack's record, and consistent with the listing: a variadic call site in this ABI must reserve and clean the register-save area with an immediate, and this body pushes nothing before its first call.

entry_paths: 0x013f5800: a dword in the table based at 0x013f57f8, at displacement +0x08. Read from the table's own bytes: /read_memory at 0x013f57f8 for 32 bytes returns 90 24 5b 00 | d0 a0 5b 00 | f0 d6 57 00 | f0 fb b1 00 | 00 43 58 00 | 50 6c 57 00 | d0 e6 58 00 | 20 7a 58 00, i.e. slots 0 and 1 hold 0x005b2490 and 0x005ba0d0 and slot 2 holds 0x0057d6f0.
mechanics.entry_path_note: There is no direct caller. All four code references are one table slot and three this-adjusting stubs, and the stubs are themselves reachable only as table entries. So the body is a leaf entered only through its slot and the three adjustors, never called by name in this image. That is a statement about the entry paths, not a claim that nothing calls it: an indirect call through a table slot has no static edge, and the pack's callers list is empty while the xref export records four references. Those three stubs are also the caller-side corroboration of the __thiscall determination: a first argument a caller-side stub reduces by a constant is a receiver, and the derived record's own "corroboration": "not_available" is supplied by them.
mechanics.callee_0x00579e20: 649 instructions. Entered with the object in ECX and no stack argument; begins PUSH ECX / PUSH EBX / PUSH ESI / MOV ESI,ECX / XOR EBX,EBX and ends POP ESI / POP EBX / POP ECX / RET. Its FIRST act is `MOV dword ptr [ESI],0x13f57f8` at 0x00579e27: it installs the very table 0x013f57f8 that this body occupies at slot +0x08. It then releases a long series of members -- calls to 0x00f47380 guarded by `CMP dword ptr [EAX + -0x4],EBX`, indirect calls through slot +0x04 and +0x08 of various objects, refcount work through XADD.LOCK -- and finishes by re-pointing the object's leading words at 0x013eb938 (offsets 0x00 and 0x04) and 0x13ec458 / 0x13eb394 (offsets 0x14 and 0x10). Described as teardown because that is what those instructions do; it is NOT declared a C++ destructor, because the SDK never named it and this binary carries no MSVC RTTI. It clobbers EAX, ECX and EDX, which is exactly why this body carries the receiver in ESI.
mechanics.callee_0x00f47380: seven instructions: MOV EAX,dword ptr [ESP + 0x4] ; TEST EAX,EAX ; JZ 0x00f47394 ; MOV ECX,dword ptr [0x016c8b44] ; PUSH EAX ; CALL 0x009276c0 ; RET. So one cdecl stack argument, a null test on it, and no stack cleanup -- the bare C3 at 0x00f47394 is why the listing needs ADD ESP,0x4 at 0x0057d705. Described as dispose; no role beyond that is claimed, and its absolute 0x016c8b44 is not modelled here.
mechanics.stack_arithmetic: With E the callee's entry ESP: PUSH ESI gives E-4; 0x00579e20 returns with a bare RET and no argument consumed, so E-4; the TEST at 0x0057d6f8 therefore reads the byte at E+4, which is the low byte of the caller's first ordinary stack argument, the return address occupying E..E+3. PUSH ESI gives E-8; 0x00f47380 returns with a bare RET, so E-8; ADD ESP,0x4 gives E-4; POP ESI gives E; RET 0x4 leaves the caller at E+4, so four bytes of stack argument are consumed on the callee side. This is the pack's {stack_cleanup_bytes 4, stack_cleanup_owner callee, evidence 'ret 0x4', confidence OBSERVED}, re-derived from the terminators rather than copied from it.
mechanics.reach_of_the_esi_save: The save at 0x0057d6f0 and the restore at 0x0057d70a are a pair around the whole body. Nothing writes ESI between 0x0057d6f1 and 0x0057d708 except the PUSH at 0x0057d6ff, which is balanced by 0x00f47380's own return. That is why `MOV EAX,ESI` at 0x0057d708 -- the sole write to EAX, and reached by both paths because the JZ target is 0x0057d708 -- returns the receiver and neither callee's result.

semantic_findings: The body is a two-step teardown: run the object's own teardown unconditionally, then, only if bit 0 of the option word is set, hand the same object to a one-argument disposer, and return the object either way. The order is machine-fixed (teardown first, unconditionally) and the model test measures it.

The object pointer is the same value at all three places it appears: the teardown's argument, the disposer's argument, and EAX on return. The body never adjusts it, even though it is reached through three stubs that adjust ECX by 0x10, 0x14 and 0x4 -- so the object the body operates on is the sub-object its caller named, not the head of anything.
The option word is read once, as one bit of one byte, and is never passed on. No callee receives it. So whatever selects the dispose is consumed here and does not reach either routine.

The returned value is a pointer to an object this function has just torn down, and on the disposing path has just handed to a disposer. Whether the caller is entitled to it is a question this body does not answer, and the body offers no evidence either way: nothing here tests for null before either call and nothing here tests the result afterwards.

The teardown routine installs the same table this body occupies. That is a machine fact about two addresses, and it is the strongest thing available here towards saying these two routines are about one class. It is not a class name and none is asserted.
unresolved_questions: Whether the INFERRED convention is the right one in an absolute sense. The derived record DETERMINES __thiscall (rule R1-VFT for the receiver, rule C6B for the convention) and this package carries that determination verbatim; it does not claim more than the record. What is not settled is anything the record itself does not cover: no caller dispatching through the table at 0x013f57f8 has been observed in this repository, so the confidence stays INFERRED and is carried as such in observed_original_abi.calling_convention_confidence. A concrete caller-side observation (a run-time trace, or a caller other than the three this-adjusting stubs) would move this from inferred to observed, and nothing here pretends otherwise.

Whether the receiver record can ever enumerate an offset for this body. abi_derived.receiver is now present and names ECX, so the validator CAN scan the listing under that register -- and the scan finds nothing, because the eleven instructions contain no displacement through ECX at all. That absence is the honest answer and is now adjudicated (FIELDS/OFFSETS passes on the register-agnostic absence arm, over the complete 11-instruction parse). What remains open is the other direction: this body can never GROW a field claim from its own bytes, and any offset a future reader wants to attribute to the receiver has to come from a callee or from a class analysis, neither of which is imported here.
